title: Localization is preserved by an equivalence of the target
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal L,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], let $S$ be a class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$, and let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$ be a localization at $S$ in the functor-category universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Let $E:\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal D$ be an equivalence, given by a functor with a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms for both composites. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor and $\eta:E\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ a natural isomorphism. Then $F$ is a localization at $S$ in the same sense, including inversion of $S$ and the equivalence of functor categories for every target category. All categories fit in a common sufficiently large universe.
